goal: Make the built-in AI Assistant an instance of AgentSpec and make the public runtime API the only contract every surface uses, so a new product form or capability can be added without changing the agent kernel.
last_result: Program scaffolded from the platform architecture review on 2026-08-14. No implementation has started; every feature is still failing by definition.
next_action: None — program superseded by the Rust kernel migration (agent-runtime-full-rust-cutover); see the note in superseded_by. Do not resume this loop without a new PRD.

features.description: AgentSpec can declare mode, a permission ruleset, and a run budget, while existing capability bindings keep working unchanged.
steps: Load an AgentSpec JSON that has no mode, permissions, or budget field.
Observe it still deserializes and resolves with mode defaulting to primary and an empty ruleset.
Load an AgentSpec that declares mode=subagent, a deny rule, and steps=8.
Observe the ruleset denies the matching tool and the budget is carried into the resolved spec.

features.description: The built-in assistant's behaviour is fully described by one exported default AgentSpec, and an agent created from that spec behaves the same.
steps: Export the default assistant spec through the agents API.
Create a new agent from the exported spec.
Send the same prompt to the built-in assistant and to that agent.
Observe the same tool advertisement set, the same system prompt sections, and the same thinking policy.

features.description: Knowledge, skill, and execution settings are resolved from the agent spec, and a chat request only carries what an end user decides during the conversation.
steps: Create an agent whose spec sets kb bindings, skills, and an execution profile.
Send a chat request that carries none of those fields.
Observe the run uses the spec's values.
Send a legacy request that still carries kb_top_k and observe it is honoured and reported as deprecated.

features.description: A subagent is described by an AgentSpec with mode=subagent rather than by bespoke dispatch code.
steps: Define a subagent as an AgentSpec with mode=subagent and a restricted ruleset.
Spawn it from a parent run.
Observe the child honours its own ruleset and budget, and that depth limits and approval fail-closed behaviour are unchanged.

features.description: The web console reaches the assistant through the same public runtime contract an embedded widget uses.
steps: Open the console assistant page and send a message.
Observe the network calls go to the public runtime endpoints, not to a console-only path.
Load the embed widget against the same agent and observe an equivalent event stream.

features.description: A client SDK can run an agent through the public runtime contract, including streaming and feedback, without gateway console credentials.
steps: Use the SDK to fetch a public agent config by public id.
Start a streaming run and consume events to completion.
Submit feedback for that run.
Observe channel policy is enforced for a disallowed origin.

features.description: Adding a surface or a capability is described by a document, and a gate fails when domain logic lands in the shared core package.
steps: Read the adding-a-surface and adding-a-capability documents.
Follow them to register a trivial no-op surface and a trivial capability.
Add a domain module under packages/ai-gateway-core and observe make harness-check fails.
Remove it and observe the gate passes.

superseded_by: agent-runtime-full-rust-cutover (Rust single kernel owns the assistant loop); ACU-00 never started; its AgentSpec contract direction was overtaken by the single-kernel migration.
